title: Structural pseudo-classes: first/last/nth child and of-type
learningObjectives: Explain structural pseudo-classes: first/last/nth child and of-type and write selectors that match the intended elements.

understand.concept: Structural pseudo-classes select elements based on their position among siblings. :first-child and :last-child select boundary children; :nth-child() accepts an An+B formula; :first-of-type and :nth-of-type() count siblings of the same element type.
understand.whyItMatters: Structural selectors reduce extra classes for repeated patterns, but their result depends on the actual DOM structure. Inserting a new sibling can change which item matches nth-child().
understand.analogy: These selectors are like choosing positions in a queue: first, last, every second, or the first item of a particular category.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; selector matching and specificity follow the CSS selector and cascade rules.

explain.narrative: The first item is bold, even items have a background, and the final item has a bottom border.

examples.explanation: The first item is bold, even items have a background, and the final item has a bottom border.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser applies the styles to elements that match the selectors.

practise.guidedTask: Change nth-child(even) to nth-child(3n). Add a different element type among the siblings and compare nth-child with nth-of-type.
practise.independentTask: Create a small document with several matching and non-matching elements. Write selectors for the required states and verify them in developer tools.
hints: Inspect which elements match each selector.
Keep selectors readable and tied to stable semantics.

questions.prompt: Which pseudo-class selects every second matching sibling in an alternating pattern?
questions.explanation: nth-child(even) selects children at even positions.
